files.purpose: Derivation-boundary secret redaction for capture-DERIVED artifacts (template drafts, review candidates, offline summaries) before they become durable. Content-driven (never key-name driven): email/JWT/signed-URL-query/userinfo/kv-secret/opaque-token detectors + a profile-aware capture scrub (redact_capture) and the build-gate proof scanner (scan_floor_secrets) that fails the WACZ export on any floor residual.
files.data_flow: derived-artifact/assembled-capture dict -> per-string content detectors -> redacted copy (PLACEHOLDER) ; scanner returns [(json_path, kind)] residuals (kinds never values). All detectors ReDoS-bounded ({m,n}); recursion depth-capped (_MAX_WALK_DEPTH=500, deep-DOM guard).
files.notes: I0008 (KV keyword set derived from the SoT SENSITIVE_QS_KEY, minus signing-metadata, plus header-origin csrf/xsrf/bearer) is correctly implemented in _kv_key_is_secret (the VR-P03 fix). NON-JSON-LEAF FAIL-CLOSED: scan_artifact_secrets / scan_floor_secrets silently skip bytes/set leaves; this is acceptable here only because (a) inputs are JSON-derived structures and (b) the WACZ json.dumps boundary (wacz_export:160) raises TypeError on a non-JSON leaf -> export fail-closes, and the canonical bytes/set fail-closed fix lives upstream in capture_redact.scrub_globals (guarded by test_v3_66_529). INVARIANT-GRAPH NOTE: I0010's 'at' field points here but its fix+guard are in capture_redact.py (P6).

files.purpose: Opt-in (BD_CAPTURE_BODIES, default OFF) response-body retention with a capture-TIME body redactor. Only text/*, JSON, and HLS/DASH manifest content types are ever stored; binary/stream bytes stay a length marker. Two-sided redaction (key-name SoT + value-shape jwt/long-token/signed-URL detectors) so a JWT under an innocent key is still masked.
files.data_flow: response body + content-type -> eligibility gate (flag + type) -> JSON path: parse, _redact_json (depth<=8), re-serialize, size-capped ; text path: _redact_text token scrub, char-capped. Ineligible/oversize -> body_marker length marker.

files.purpose: Append-only, tamper-evident provenance ledger (one immutable row per completed download) with a Merkle-like chain hash. Insert + query + O(n) chain verification; no update/delete API by policy.
files.data_flow: download metadata -> _row_content_hash (sorted-key JSON) -> _chain_hash(prev||content) -> parameterized INSERT. query() builds a dynamic WHERE by appending only CONSTANT ' AND col = ?' fragments with every value bound as a ? param.
files.notes: INJECTION CLEAR: the 12 'sql_sites' flagged by the graph are the safe parameterized dynamic-WHERE pattern (constant fragments, bound values) -- no user input is ever concatenated into SQL text. :91 'sql_fstring' is a FALSE POSITIVE (a sys.stderr.write error-message f-string inside _ensure_table, attributed to the enclosing cx.execute context). DDL is static IF NOT EXISTS. Fail-open on every DB op is documented/intended (losing audit data < failing a download); verify_chain is the tamper-evident backstop.

files.purpose: WACZ 1.1.1-shaped ZIP packager (stdlib zipfile+hashlib, no third-party dep). Runs a defense-in-depth profile-aware export-boundary scrub, stamps the active redaction profile + a value-free capture-health block, and FAILS CLOSED (WaczRedactionError, carrying kinds-not-values) if any floor secret would reach capture.json.
files.data_flow: capture dict -> redact_capture(copy) -> scan_floor_secrets -> [residual? -> _force_scrub_floor + re-scan -> still residual? RAISE] -> json.dumps -> STORED zip with per-resource sha256 digests + datapackage-digest.
files.notes: FAIL-CLOSED floor: the force-scrub-then-re-scan-then-raise path is the strict floor guarantee. The json.dumps(capture) at :160 is the serialization backstop that fail-closes on a bytes/set leaf (TypeError aborts export) -- this is what backstops the artifact-scanner non-JSON-leaf gap noted on capture_artifact_redact. path_sink :202 = open(out_path,'wb') with a caller-controlled export destination (no web taint).

files.purpose: Live cam-stream recorder: parse_live_url host-matches known cam sites, watch() arms a Recording, a scheduler probes liveness (streamlink --json) and spawns streamlink/ffmpeg to record to disk, with disk-pressure gating, a max-active cap, dedupe, and SIGTERM->SIGKILL teardown. State persisted to recordings.json.
files.data_flow: url -> watch(): parse_live_url host-allowlist (SKIPPED when site_override+room_override both given) + UNCONDITIONAL ^https?://...$ shape check -> Recording(url=...). scheduler -> _is_room_live(rec.url) [streamlink --json LIST-form] -> _build_cmd(rec.url) [streamlink/ffmpeg LIST-form, re-validates ^https?://] -> Popen(shell=False).
files.notes: Both subprocess sites are LIST-form shell=False (682 streamlink --json, 744 Popen(cmd)) -> no shell injection. Argument injection is closed: rec.url is entry-validated ^https?://...$ at BOTH population paths (watch():435 AND _load_state() rehydration -- both added by a prior audit v3.43.62, with explicit 'recordings.json is user-writable, do not trust' reasoning), so rec.url can never be read as a -flag. room slug allowlisted (_looks_like_safe_room). See finding F-CAP01-01 for the SSRF residual on the override path.

findings.title: watch() site_override+room_override path bypasses the cam-site HOST allowlist (validates URL shape only) -> streamlink/ffmpeg will fetch any http(s) host
findings.detail: On the normal path, parse_live_url restricts the URL host to known cam sites via _SITE_PATTERNS. When BOTH site_override and room_override are supplied, parse_live_url is SKIPPED (line 421) and the only remaining gate is the ^https?://[A-Za-z0-9.\-/_?=&%:]+$ SHAPE check (435). A shape-valid but arbitrary-host URL (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/, http://localhost:5555/..., a private-range host) is then stored as rec.url and handed to streamlink (_is_room_live: 'streamlink --json <url>') and to ffmpeg/streamlink in _build_cmd -> the server fetches an operator-attacker-chosen internal URL. This is classic SSRF surface. It is NOT shell/argument injection (list-form, shape-validated leading scheme), so the graph's mechanical scanner (shell=false) reported the subprocess as safe and missed it. [WITNESS W6 CONFIRMED at the live_recorder boundary: watch(site_override,room_override) accepts a link-local metadata IP. Capability proven; only cross-batch route reachability remains to set final severity.]
findings.fix: On the override path, still constrain the URL host: require parse_live_url to recognize the host (reject overrides for an unknown host), OR add an explicit SSRF guard (reject private/loopback/link-local/metadata IPs via ipaddress.is_global, mirroring I0003's provider_resolve classifier) before storing rec.url. Apply the same host check in both watch() and _load_state().
findings.repro_test: tests/test_live_recorder_ssrf_override_host.py::test_override_rejects_non_cam_host (TO WRITE in the serial fix-cut; RED on pristine 532)
findings.reachability_note: Reachability + true severity depend on the APP-layer route that calls watch(): (a) is it behind the operator auth gate, and (b) are site_override/room_override exposed to that caller? That wiring is in the APP batch (app_*.py), not CAP-01. Recorded as TRIAGE pending the cross-batch route audit; do not fix in isolation until reachability is confirmed.

new_invariants.statement: Any url stored in a live_recorder Recording must be entry-validated to ^https?://...$ before it can reach a subprocess argv. Both population paths (watch() and _load_state() rehydration) must enforce it; _is_room_live relies on this invariant rather than re-validating.
new_invariants.promote_note: Currently enforced by convention at watch():435 and _load_state():(rehydration re-check). UNGUARDED until a serial fix-cut adds a RED guard asserting BOTH paths reject a non-^https?:// url and that no Recording with a bad url reaches _build_cmd/_is_room_live. Pairs with the F-CAP01-01 host-allowlist fix (extend the same guard to assert host constraint).

new_patterns.rule: list-form subprocess (shell=False) is NOT sufficient to clear a URL/path argv element: also require the value to be shape-validated so it cannot be read as an option (argument injection) AND host-constrained if it triggers a network fetch (SSRF). Flag a subprocess argv element that is a request-derived URL whose host is not allowlisted.
new_patterns.signature: subprocess.run/Popen([...]) with shell=False where an argv element is a URL var that reaches the network and whose host validation is bypassable
new_patterns.note: Refinement of the existing subprocess detector: shell=false currently scores the site safe, which is why F-CAP01-01 was a manual-only catch. Promote to defect_patterns after confirming on the F-CAP01-01 repro.
